    Watermark detection

    AI-content detection — bring your own detector

    The FOSS core ships the public Detector trait and dispatch registry, but no classifier weights. That is deliberate — provcheck does not bundle any commercial model, and no open-source AI-content detector currently meets our license policy (both code AND weights permissive).

    Route A — paid DLC pack (v1.x, planned)

    Creative Mayhem will offer a paid detector pack layered on top of the FOSS core. Install through provcheck-kit dlc install ai-detect; the pack registers a detector against the trait and this tab lights up.

    Route B — operator-supplied wrapper (available now)

    Any Apache-2.0 wrapper crate that implements provcheck_detect::Detector can register itself via DetectorRegistry::register in a fork of app/src-tauri/src/main.rs. Full trait contract lives in docs/public-api-stability.md.

    Not to be confused with the Watermark tab — that surface detects embedded provenance marks put there by a known generator at render time (silentcipher, TrustMark, SynthID-text) and does ship live in the FOSS core.

    Set up your signing identity

    This generates a cryptographic key on this machine and stores it in your OS keychain. You'll only need to do this once.

    The key never leaves your machine. Your OS handles access prompts.

    Connect your bsky identity

    Attach your signing key to your atproto handle so verifiers know it's yours.

    App passwords are scoped tokens — generate one at bsky.app → Settings → App Passwords. Never paste your account password here.

    Publish your signing key

    One last step — publishing your key's fingerprint to atproto lets verifiers cross-check that you signed your work. Without this they only see "valid signature by unknown."

    Or — works, but no atproto attestation.

    Your signing key is out of date

    This box's local key is marked retired on atproto. Verifiers won't attest signatures from it.

      How Backfire works
      
        
      
      
      
      
        
      
          Backfire is a keyed, per-image watermark that AI provenance strippers
          amplify instead of erase. A "regeneration" attack runs an image back
          through a diffusion model to strip ordinary watermarks. Backfire instead optimizes
          its mark to be a fixed point of that attack, so running the stripper makes
          the keyed identifier read stronger. The attack backfires.
        
      

        
      Using this tab
      
        
        
          
      1. Enter the key the mark was embedded with. Backfire is keyed:
            you can only read a mark made with your key.
        2. 
          
      2. Drop an image, or click Choose file. It never leaves
            your machine.
        3. 
          
      3. Backfire reads the keyed identifier and reports the result below.
        4. 
        
      

        
      The fields
      
        
        
          
      • Key (required) — the secret the mark was written with.
        • 
          
      • Expected serial (optional) — a specific id such as
            0x7 to check for; the result then says whether it matched.
        • 
          
      • Carriers — must match how the image was marked. Leave
            band unless it was embedded with edge.
        • 
        
      

        
      The result
      
        
        
          
      • Identifier — the recovered id (0x0–0xF).
        • 
          
      • Confidence — how far the read clears the validity
            threshold. A genuine mark clears it with room; an unmarked or wrong-key image
            reads near the floor.
        • 
          
      • Tamper tripwire — flags if the image was band-notched.
            That is the one attack that can strip the mark, and it leaves a loud spectral
            hole this detects.
        • 
        
      

        
      
          Experimental research. This tab reads marks only. Creating
          a mark (embedding) is a separate, GPU-bound step run with the standalone Backfire
          tool, which is BUSL-licensed (free for non-commercial use) and separate from
          provcheck. Robustness is per-image
          and the method is early; treat results as experimental.
        
      
        
      
          Full documentation, reproduction scripts, and the honest limits (self-red-team):
          github.com/CreativeMayhemLtd/provcheck/backfire
